The *Paṭhamasatta Sutta* (Ud 7.3, PTS Ud 75) is a short canonical discourse located in the seventh chapter of the *Udāna*. The core teaching of the sutta addresses the danger of attachment to sensual pleasures, illustrating how such attachment prevents one from crossing over the flood. Within later exegetical and paracanonical literature, the sutta is cited or referenced in the *Peṭakopadesa* (Pe 1 and Pe 2).

Curated passage-level verse parallels are preserved in several recensions of the *Udānavarga*, including the Sanskrit *Paśyavarga* (UV 27, UVS 27), the Tibetan translation (Uv Kg 27), and Chinese parallels found in the *Chu yao jing* (T 212.28) and the *Fa ji yao song jing* (T 213.27).
